/-!
# Conjecture 1.5

by L. A. Bokut'

(Well-known problem). Does there exist a group whose group ring does not contain
zero divisors and is not embeddable into a skew field?

The notebook does not specify the coefficient ring of the group ring. We take the
integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$. This agrees with the version over $\mathbb{Q}$:
$\mathbb{Z}[G]$ has no zero divisors if and only if $\mathbb{Q}[G]$ has none, and
$\mathbb{Z}[G]$ embeds into a skew field if and only if $\mathbb{Q}[G]$ does.
A skew field is a not necessarily commutative division ring.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

theorem kourovka.«1.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsDomain (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) ∧
      ¬ ∃ (D : Type) (_ : DivisionRing D) (f : MonoidAlgebra ℤ G →+* D),
        Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

Does there exist a group $G$ whose group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$ does not contain zero
divisors and is not embeddable into a skew field?

The group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$ is nontrivial, so "does not contain zero divisors" is
stated as `IsDomain`. "Embeddable into a skew field" means that there is an injective
ring homomorphism from $\mathbb{Z}[G]$ into some (not necessarily commutative) division
ring $D$.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no existence question (∃ group G with the group ring a domain, i.e. nontrivial with no zero divisors, and no injective ring hom into any division ring); the coefficient ring of the 'group ring' is left unspecified by the notebook (classically ℤ[G], or K[G] for a field K — note ℤ[G] embeds in a skew field iff ℚ[G] does), so the formalization must fix and document a choice, and 'skew field' means a not-necessarily-commutative division ring.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition: ∃ group G with ℤ[G] a domain and no injective (unital) ring hom into any DivisionRing. c03's form is chosen as the cleanest: inline (no unneeded bespoke definition as in c01), uses `IsDomain` (explicitly nontrivial + no zero divisors, matching the decomposition note; verified in a scratch file to be equivalent to `NoZeroDivisors` for `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G`, so c04/c06/c07's `Nontrivial ∧ NoZeroDivisors` and c05's bare `NoZeroDivisors` are equivalent but either redundant or less explicit), follows the `∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), …` idiom of Kourovka/1_74.lean, and documents the ℤ-coefficient choice with the correct ℤ[G] ≡ ℚ[G] remark. c02/c03/c08 have identical declarations; c03 was used verbatim (no edits needed), c02's and c01's/c05's extra `variants.field` declarations were not shipped.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 1.5

by L. A. Bokut'

(Well-known problem). Does there exist a group whose group ring does not contain
zero divisors and is not embeddable into a skew field?

The notebook does not specify the coefficient ring of the group ring. We take the
integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$. This agrees with the version over $\mathbb{Q}$:
$\mathbb{Z}[G]$ has no zero divisors if and only if $\mathbb{Q}[G]$ has none, and
$\mathbb{Z}[G]$ embeds into a skew field if and only if $\mathbb{Q}[G]$ does.
A skew field is a not necessarily commutative division ring.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.5»

/--
Does there exist a group $G$ whose group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$ does not contain zero
divisors and is not embeddable into a skew field?

The group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$ is nontrivial, so "does not contain zero divisors" is
stated as `IsDomain`. "Embeddable into a skew field" means that there is an injective
ring homomorphism from $\mathbb{Z}[G]$ into some (not necessarily commutative) division
ring $D$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 16 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsDomain (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) ∧
      ¬ ∃ (D : Type) (_ : DivisionRing D) (f : MonoidAlgebra ℤ G →+* D),
        Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.5»

items: Coefficient ring of the unspecified 'group ring' is fixed as ℤ (the integral group ring ℤ[G] = `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G`), documented in the module docstring. This coincides with the ℚ[G] reading: ℤ[G] has no zero divisors iff ℚ[G] has none (clear denominators via the central subring ℤ), and ℤ[G] embeds in a skew field iff ℚ[G] does. A reading with an arbitrary field K (∃ K, ∃ G) is a priori not equivalent (a positive answer only in positive characteristic would be missed); the ℤ reading is the canonical 'the group ring of G' in group-theoretic usage.

'Does not contain zero divisors' is stated as `IsDomain (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G)`. Since the group ring over ℤ is nontrivial (instance exists), this is equivalent to `NoZeroDivisors (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G)`; checked in a scratch file.
'Skew field' is `DivisionRing` (Mathlib's not-necessarily-commutative division ring), not `Field`.
'Embeddable' is an injective unital ring homomorphism `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G →+* D`. Ring homs are unital, which is the standard meaning of a ring embedding into a skew field.

Both G and the target division ring D live in `Type` (repo convention). Restricting D to `Type` loses nothing: if ℤ[G] embeds in a division ring in any universe, the division subring generated by the image has cardinality ≤ max(|ℤ[G]|, ℵ₀), hence is equivalent to a type in `Type`.

Degeneracy check: the trivial group is not a witness (ℤ[1] ≅ ℤ embeds in ℚ), so the existential is not trivially satisfied; the conjunction `IsDomain … ∧ ¬ …` (rather than an implication) avoids vacuous truth.
AMS tags 16 (associative rings) and 20 (group theory); category `research open` per the status given.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity: the notebook does not fix the coefficient ring of the 'group ring'. The final file fixes ℤ[G] (= MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) and documents that this is equivalent to the ℚ[G] reading (ℤ[G] is a domain iff ℚ[G] is; ℤ[G] embeds in a skew field iff ℚ[G] does, since any division ring containing ℤ has char 0 and the central localization extends the embedding). The reading 'K[G] for some field K' (∃ K) is a priori a different question; three candidates (c01, c02, c05) added it as `kourovka.«1.5».variants.field`. It is not a slot in the decomposition table, so per the instruction to ship exactly the surviving slots it was omitted; a maintainer may wish to add it as a documented variant. Other checks: DivisionRing in Mathlib is not-necessarily-commutative (noncommutative instances exist, e.g. quaternions), so 'skew field' is correctly modeled; unital `→+*` loses nothing since an injective non-unital ring hom into a division ring is automatically unital; D : Type (universe 0) loses nothing since the division subring generated by the image of ℤ[G] has small cardinality; the trivial group is not a witness; conditions are conjoined so no vacuous truth; answer(True)/answer(False) correspond to positive/negative answers. No candidate omitted the slot; all compiled. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
